title: Explicit Closed-Form ex(n; K₂,ₜ) from the Kővári–Sós–Turán Quadratic

problemStatement.formal: For fixed $t \ge 2$, a $K_{2,t}$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges satisfies the Kővári–Sós–Turán quadratic $4m^2 \le (t-1)\,n^2(n-1) + 2nm$, whence $m \le \tfrac14\,n\bigl(1 + \sqrt{\,1 + 4(t-1)(n-1)\,}\bigr)$.
problemStatement.plain: The parent entry solved the quadratic that bounds the edges of a C₄-free (K₂,₂-free) graph, turning $4m^2 \le n^2(n-1) + 2nm$ into the explicit Reiman form $m \le \tfrac14 n(1+\sqrt{4n-3})$. This problem asks for the same explicit form one step more general: for a $K_{2,t}$-free graph the Kővári–Sós–Turán count produces a quadratic $4m^2 \le (t-1)n^2(n-1) + 2nm$ with the parameter $t-1$ in front, and we want the clean closed form $m \le \tfrac14 n(1 + \sqrt{1 + 4(t-1)(n-1)})$. The goal is a single parametric Lean 4 lemma recovering the sharp upper root of this $t$-dependent quadratic and specializing back to $C_4$ at $t=2$.
whyMatters: $K_{2,t}$-free extremal numbers are the next rung of the Zarankiewicz ladder above $C_4$: Kővári–Sós–Turán (1954) give $\text{ex}(n;K_{2,t}) \le \tfrac12(\sqrt{t-1}\,n^{3/2}+n)$ and Füredi (1996) proved this asymptotically tight, $\text{ex}(n;K_{2,t}) = \tfrac12\sqrt{t-1}\,n^{3/2}(1+o(1))$.
A machine-checked solved quadratic gives the precise finite-$n$ constant rather than an asymptotic estimate.

It shows the parent's sqrt-free quadratic-solving mechanism (reiman_quadratic_solve) generalizes verbatim to a whole family of extremal problems, and it feeds the density thresholds governing Erdős #1008.

open: The $t$-parametric quadratic $4m^2 \le (t-1)n^2(n-1) + 2nm$ has not been solved to explicit closed form in Lean.
The general discriminant identity $s^2 = 1 + 4(t-1)(n-1)$ (reducing to $4n-3$ at $t=2$) is not yet formalized.
The counting derivation of the $K_{2,t}$ quadratic itself ($\sum_v \binom{\deg v}{2} \le (t-1)\binom{n}{2}$) is outside the parent scope.
knownResults.goal: Formalize a parametric lemma kst_quadratic_solve generalizing reiman_quadratic_solve: for reals $m,n,s\ge 0$ with $n\ge 1$, $c = t-1 \ge 1$, and $s^2 = 1 + 4c(n-1)$ with $4m^2 \le c\,n^2(n-1) + 2nm$, prove $4m \le n(1+s)$; then specialize to $c=1$ to recover the Reiman bound and confirm the discriminant collapses to $4n-3$.

insights: The C4 algebraic core generalises to K_{2,t} with zero structural change: replace the single-common-neighbour bound by (t-1), so s^2=4n-3 becomes s^2=1+4(t-1)(n-1) and the KST quadratic gains a (t-1) factor on the n^2(n-1) term. Same nlinarith case-split proof works.
Leading-order closed form is ex(n;K_{2,t}) <= (1/2)(sqrt(t-1)*n^{3/2}+n), matching the classical Kovari-Sos-Turan asymptotic.
